text:
maya: customer on windows+corporate proxy hitting sampleapp stream crash. stack trace points to "TextDecoder.decode" throwing on chunk boundary.
eli: thrown how? invalid start byte?
maya: yes. server logs show chunk split inside a multi-byte utf8 char. pasted trimmed stream capture: 
```
2026-03-21T09:10:01.001Z OUT chunk="data: {"id":10,"text":"Hi "}"
2026-03-21T09:10:01.002Z OUT chunk="data: {"id":10,"text":"\xF0\x9F\x98"}"
2026-03-21T09:10:01.003Z OUT chunk="data: {"id":10,"text":"\x8A"}"
```
maya: that last EMOJI byte separated by proxy buffering causes decoder.decode to error if used on partial bytes. sampleapp's stream util does naive decode per chunk.
sam: oof. we saw something similar but assumed rare. Did the client try to combine chunks before decoding?
maya: no, browser path decodes per-read; node path accumulated bytes. so parity gap again.
el i: two issues here: 1) don't call TextDecoder.decode on arbitrary byte slices without streaming mode, 2) blank events (\n\n) are sometimes emitted by proxy leading to duplicate event handling.
jonah: for streaming TextDecoder, use new TextDecoder().decode(value, {stream:true}) to avoid error on incomplete sequences and then finalize at end with stream:false. also keep an internal Uint8Array buffer for leftover partial bytes.
sam: for EventSource parity, we need same behavior for fetch-based SSE and EventSource-based path. EventSource buffers more of this for us, so sampleapp differs. add small shim: decode streaming + coalesce until we hit double-newline or explicit event id marker.
maya: another wrinkle: when we re-auth (token refresh), we open a new connection and the server sometimes emits a comment `:resume <token>` then resumes. some clients merged leftover partial bytes from previous connection into the resumed stream — leading to concatenated JSON objects without delimiter. we should treat comment markers as parser reset points.
eli: agree. proposed changes: 1) streaming-safe TextDecoder usage + leftover buffer, 2) ignore empty events (blank lines), 3) reset parser buffer on `:` comment lines that indicate auth/resume, 4) unify behavior across SDKs.
sam: I'll draft a tiny parser util and export for node/browser. API: createSseParser({onEvent, onComment}) that handles stream:true decode, byte buffer, balanced-brace heuristic, and accepts explicit reset().
jonah: add an integration test: proxy-mock that injects random CRLFs and splits utf8 codepoints mid-emission; test both browser and node harnesses. mark flaky tolerance threshold.
ci-bot: test-run queued: sampleapp-integration/utf8-proxy-split across win/chrome, nodejs 18.
devx-bot: created RDW-1920: "sampleapp: tolerate utf8 splits and proxy-inserted blank events; reset on :resume marker" and assigned to sam + eli.
maya: customer gave temporary workaround: enable "preserve-encoding" at proxy (not ideal). we'll follow up with post-fix note for onboarding docs.
eli: can we also surface a short troubleshooting blurb in sampleapp readme about proxies and SSE pitfalls? I can draft after PR lands.
sam: PR will include parser util, docs snippet, and tests. aiming for end of day. :rocket:
